A1.justification: Both PDFs contain readable main texts and complete Appendices A–C describing the same research. The transformer construction, main theorems, and proofs can be matched across renumbering and reformatting.

before.justification: Section 4 reports a qualitative outcome attributed to the authors' numerical results: increasing transformer depth improves prediction. This empirical reporting is minimal; no experimental setup, numerical values, or plots accompany the statement.

after.justification: Section 4 and Figure 1 report original simulation results for trained linear and softmax transformers at depths 1–5. These clearly establish empirical content despite the checklist's contradictory statements that the paper contains no experiments.

M1.justification: The linear-transformer architecture, four-block token embedding, training objective, Richardson-iteration construction, and restricted single-layer predictor remain unchanged. Softmax attention appears in the new empirical comparison, without replacing the proposed construction.

E1.justification: v3 explicitly identifies evaluation on simulated noisy one-dimensional linear dynamical systems. v1's numerical-results statement does not identify its evaluation data, so the PDFs cannot establish whether this expands empirical coverage or first documents the same coverage.

E2.justification: Figure 1 newly reports softmax-attention models alongside linear-attention models, with depths 1–5 for each family. v1 contains no corresponding reported comparator set. Least squares remains a theoretical reference rather than an evaluated numerical baseline.

E3.justification: v3 first specifies T = 500, w in [0, 0.8], depths 1–5, task-averaged test error, and curves covering 1,000 epochs. Because v1 supplies no protocol for its claimed numerical results, these cannot reliably be distinguished from newly disclosed settings of an existing experiment. The theoretical uniform-over-tasks loss is unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4 and Figure 1 add substantive depth-sensitivity evidence for both attention families, examining the separation between one and multiple layers and the benefits of further depth. v1 only asserts a general numerical depth benefit without presenting the corresponding analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The newly displayed curves have no uncertainty bands; checklist guidance about statistical reporting does not supply actual statistical evidence.

E6.justification: Figure 1 adds ten test-MSE curves. Both attention families show substantially higher loss at depth 1; linear models have similar losses at depths 2–5, while softmax models improve with depth through 5. These detailed results extend v1's generic depth-benefit statement, without establishing a same-setting performance improvement between versions.

T1.justification: The limiting-loss expression changes from +w in v1's Lemma 1 to −w in v3's Proposition 1, with corresponding corrections in the proof sketch and several Appendix B equations. The main bounds and proof strategies remain unchanged. The correction is incomplete: Appendix B's Lemma 5 still displays +w.

C1.justification: The approximation bound, single-layer lower bound, and IID/non-IID distinction remain the principal contributions. v3's introduction additionally claims the first quantitative analysis of in-context population loss for non-IID data; the abstract and conclusion otherwise retain their substantive claims.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the linear-transformer depth plateau as potentially reflecting either capacity or optimization limitations and as suggesting that logarithmic depth may be unnecessary. It also contrasts continued softmax improvements with two-layer induction-head findings. Constant-depth sufficiency was already an open question in v1, but now receives empirical motivation.

D1.justification: Section 4 and Figure 1 disclose limited simulation conditions, tested depths, and the displayed training horizon; the acknowledgments add provenance for preliminary experimental code. Optimizer, learning rate, noise magnitude, hardware, and code-access instructions remain unspecified.

R1.justification: Related work substantially expands its treatment of non-IID learning and Markov chains, adding works including Wu et al. (2025), Ziemann et al. (2024), and Rajaraman et al. (2024). New positioning distinguishes noisy next-token prediction guarantees from implementing least squares, claims greater parameter efficiency, and contrasts finite-state Markov results with this paper's infinite-state setting.

P1.justification: Most existing prose is retained, with localized restructuring: results become a separate Section 3, the general single-layer extension discussion is integrated into Section 3.2, the notation subsection is removed, and related work gains thematic headings. The title and author ordering change, and numerical-experiment, acknowledgment, and checklist sections are introduced.

P2.justification: The document adopts NeurIPS formatting, changing the title and author block, typography, running headers, text density, and equation layout throughout. Figure 1 adds two panels with logarithmic MSE axes, epoch axes, and depth legends; v1 contains no corresponding empirical display.

improvement.justification: v3 makes the previously asserted numerical depth benefit inspectable in Figure 1, clarifies its relationship to prior work, and corrects several loss-sign expressions. These gains are limited by missing experimental and uncertainty details, incomplete propagation of the sign correction, and checklist answers contradicting the experimental section. The core theoretical contribution remains largely unchanged.
